messages:
Maria G: Quick heads-up — VendorCo just flagged a 2-week slip on the EU H100 allocation. ~40 units affected in the FRA staging pool. Need a triage: temporary borrower lane from APAC vs air-expedite replacements. Tagging @Jess_S @Alan_K for decisions.

Jess S: Ugh. 2 weeks kills a bunch of customer windows. Whats the pricing delta for an air-expedite swap vs borrowing? also, any customs gotchas if we move APAC units into EU temporary pool? :grimacing:

Nick (VendorCo): Sorry about the hit — confirmed: standard reallocation ETA +14 days. Options: 1) Air-expedite (DHL) — +€1,200/unit, shipped from NL hub, 4 business days. 2) APAC temporary borrower pool — $0 extra, needs cross-border temporary import docs (ATA-ish), ~7 biz days to prepare. Both need partial RMA flow for swapped serials.

Alan K: Need to know depot/dock impact. FRA staging can only ingest ~8 extra inbound units/day before we hit queue. If we choose air-expedite, we need to stagger AWBs or we'll swamp the dock.

Kevin O: FRA depot backlog is real this week. Current inbound window: Mon/Wed/Fri with 12-slot capacity. If we do air-expedite, recommend splitting into 3 AWBs with 12/14/14. Also APAC -> EU borrower requires customs broker pre-approval; that can be same-day if we have paperwork ready.

Maria G: Can you send the manifest template we need for the APAC temporary import? Ill ping legal on ATA-like docs.

Nick (VendorCo): Manifest snippet below (will supply full file):
```
AWB: 123-45678901
SKU: H100-48GB
Qty: 10
Serials: [H100-APAC-0001..0010]
Value: €1 (temporary import)
```
Also need a return-by date on the paperwork (we recommend 90 days).

Jess S: Pricing delta note: air-expedite +€1,200/unit. If we borrow from APAC we pay handling + minor brokerage (~€80/unit) and cover return shipping if units are returned damaged. Net expected savings ~€1,100/unit but with slightly longer lead.

Alan K: Operational ask: Which approach minimizes SLO risk? Air-expedite gets units in-hand fastest but risks depot swap overload. Borrower lane reduces dock spike but adds customs paperwork risk. My leaning: split approach — expedite for top 8 priority customers (8 units), borrower lane for the rest.

Kevin O: I support split. Action items for ops: 1) Reserve 3 inbound slots (AWBs) on expedite plan; 2) Pre-authorize customs broker for APAC -> EU temporary import; 3) Open RMA ticket set to "partial-swap" for serial tracking.

Maria G: Cool. @Nick, proceed with 8-unit expedite quote and prepare APAC manifest for 32 units. Please include per-unit expedite cost and expected AWB schedule.

Nick (VendorCo): Will do — sending formal quote in 30m. Also opening RMA batch id: RMA-82741 for the temporary swaps.

logistics-bot: RMA ticket created: RMA-82741. Status: open. Assignees: Alan K, Kevin O. ETA to allocate: 48h.

Jess S: One more ask — can we tag the 8 expedited units as "canary" so we can measure perf/thermal issues on arrival before rolling into prod?

Maria G: Yes, mark them canary. Also add a short checklist on preflight: firmware check, burn-in 6hr, serial reconciliation to RMA-82741.

Alan K: I'll reserve staging slots and add the checklist to the inbound playbook.

Kevin O: I'll spin up customs POC with our broker and send the required docs template to Maria and Jess in ~1 hour.

Nick (VendorCo): Quote and AWB ETA sent to email. Will attach manifest files to the RMA ticket. :thumbsup:

Maria G: Thanks team — keeping this thread as the single source of truth for the triage. Will update if legal flags the temporary import wording.
